entries.text: Cortex-M firmware ELFs (Zephyr, ZMK and similar) now disassemble as Thumb-2. The M profile recorded in `.ARM.attributes` selects the Thumb decoder for the whole file, and bit 0 of Thumb function symbol addresses (the interworking marker, not part of the real address) is stripped, so functions start at their even addresses and 32-bit wide encodings (`bl.w`, `mul.w`) decode exactly as objdump shows. Previously these files decoded as A32 from odd start addresses, producing garbage for every function. A-profile ELFs keep per-symbol mode selection: A32 by default, Thumb for symbols carrying the marker bit.

The **Debug Info** tab reported "Debug info present, but Hexana did not resolve any source line rows" for GCC-built ELFs even though `.debug_info` and `.debug_line` were present (every Zephyr/ZMK Cortex-M firmware, DWARF4 and DWARF5 alike). GCC emits DWARF version 2/3 line-program headers even in `-gdwarf-4/5` builds, and the line parser misread them with the version 4 layout, failing on the first such unit and discarding the whole section (clang and rustc emit v4/v5 headers, which always worked). Version 2/3 headers now parse, an unparseable line-table unit is skipped instead of taking the rest of the section down with it, and address-to-line resolution matches addr2line.

clusters.summary: Hexana now reads Zephyr, ZMK, and similar Cortex-M ELF firmware as Thumb-2, with correct function addresses and GCC source locations.
clusters.title: Inspect Zephyr firmware with confidence

entries.text: The **Wasm** debugger tab now works for component-model binaries: every embedded core module is indexed on its own, so the current-instruction highlight, per-instruction stepping and operand stack follow the module the runtime reports the stop in instead of assuming a single core module.

clusters.summary: The Wasm debugger now follows the embedded core module that stopped, keeping the instruction highlight, per-instruction stepping, and operand stack in sync.
clusters.title: Follow Component Model modules in the debugger

entries.text: **Run and Debug for firmware ELFs** under QEMU and Renode. Opening a Zephyr-class ELF offers Run/Debug buttons in the editor header when a target profile resolves from the ELF header plus the `zephyr.dts` and `.config` found next to it (the same build-tree discovery the Memory tab uses). QEMU boards (`qemu_cortex_m3`, `mps2/an521`, `qemu_riscv32`, `qemu_cortex_a53`, ...) launch with the exact machine flags from a curated table; MCU-class boards run under Renode, on a built-in platform where Renode ships one (nRF52840 DK, STM32F4 Discovery) or on a platform generated from the devicetree by dts2repl. The emulator choice is annotated with a recommendation and persists in the new **Hexana Firmware** run configuration; a combination the target cannot support fails at validation time naming the reason and the alternative, never as a hung emulator. Console output streams to the Run tool window behind a one-line emulation notice (unmodeled peripherals read zero, timing differs, radios are not simulated), and a startup watchdog reports "did not reach console output" naming the first unimplemented-peripheral access from the Renode log. Stop kills the whole emulator process tree; nothing is left behind on IDE exit. Debug attaches GDB in DAP mode (preferring the Zephyr SDK's `arm-zephyr-eabi-gdb-py`; minimum GDB 14 with Python) to the emulator's frozen gdb stub with a configurable stop-at-entry policy (entry, `main`, or none); an LLDB fallback covers machines without a suitable GDB. Emulator tooling is acquired on demand from the run configuration's Tools section with consent-gated, checksum-verified, cancellable downloads: the Renode 1.16.1 portable build, a per-architecture Zephyr SDK GDB toolchain, and a standalone CPython for dts2repl (all desktop platforms); each tool is also overridable by path in Settings | Build | Firmware Emulator. QEMU comes from the system package manager.

clusters.summary: Run or debug Zephyr-class firmware ELFs with QEMU or Renode, target-aware setup, and clear validation when a target combination cannot run.
clusters.title: Run and debug firmware with target-aware emulation

entries.text: **Memory** tab for ELF binaries: a section-level Flash/RAM budget view answering "how full is my device". One block per memory region with used/capacity in human units (exact bytes on hover) and a fill bar that turns yellow at 80% and red at 95%; ROM regions listed before RAM. Initialized data is annotated in both places it lives ("load image" in flash, "runtime copy" in RAM), so the totals stay explainable; `.bss` counts only toward RAM, and `noinit` sections are marked. Region capacities come from a linker map (`<name>.map`, `zephyr.map`, or any other `*.map` sibling that matches the ELF) or a Zephyr `zephyr.dts` found next to the ELF automatically, with a footer naming the source; a map whose section addresses do not match the ELF (stale build) is detected and ignored with a warning. Without any source the tab still shows the full ROM/RAM breakdown from the ELF's load segments, capacity-free, and a notification strip offers "Link capacity source..." (a `.map`, a `.dts`, or manual flash/RAM sizes; remembered per file). The budget measures address-space bytes, complementing the **Top** tab's file-byte profile: debug info that never reaches the device is excluded, and a zero-file-byte `.bss` heap arena shows up as the RAM consumer it is. Section rows navigate to the hex view. The tab appears for executable and shared-object ELFs, including fully stripped ones (no symbols or DWARF needed).

clusters.summary: The new Memory tab breaks down ELF Flash and RAM by region, explains runtime-copy data, and reads capacities from linker maps or Zephyr devicetrees.
clusters.title: See Flash and RAM budgets at a glance
